summary: The groups membership table (groups.table) decides who is in a tenant, so generic CRUD writes to it take a tenant admin unless the app declares its own rule on that table. Reads stay tenant-scoped.
tenant_admin: a global admin (users.role = admin or a group_id-NULL admin grant), bypassing or stepped into the row's tenant

a caller inside the row's tenant who passes a literal `role:admin` gate there (a tenant-scoped admin grant or a membership role named admin) or holds groups.bootstrap.founding_role (needs groups.role_field)

when no founding role is declared: the owner (user_id) of the tenant's org row - groups.bootstrap.org_table, else the table the membership table's groups.key column references. An org table without user_id leaves only the roles above
applies_to: POST /api/<groups.table> (also batch, ingest, /api/_transaction, singleton upsert), PATCH (single, batch, transaction, revert, connector update) and DELETE (single, batch, transaction). A refused write is 403 (ingest skips and counts the row). Taking a record lock on a membership row or sharing it (POST /api/<groups.table>/<id>/lock, /share) needs the same right, so a member cannot hold a rolling lock that keeps the admin from changing or removing them.
member_identity: When groups.user_field is user_id (protected: a create always fills it from the caller), a create that names anyone else answers 422 naming the field and creates nothing, admins included and whatever access rule the table declares. The same rule covers POST, batch and /api/_transaction (one bad item rolls everything back), ingest (the whole stream is refused), singleton upsert, the admin panel, and NDJSON import Mode A (the load fails; a CSV or declared column list naming user_id is refused before upload). A create that names the caller, leaves the field out or sends null works as on any other table. To add someone else, use an invitation (a row in your own invites table, accepted by the invitee) or a flow that checks who is asking and writes the membership row itself; flows and POST /api/_groups/create are not generic CRUD and are not affected. A writable groups.user_field (an email column) still takes any value, which is how an invite row names someone; its user_id column, if any, is only the row's owner and is stripped as on any table.
member_leave: A member who is not a tenant admin may still leave: DELETE their own membership row (the row whose groups.user_field names them), or PATCH only groups.active_field to an inactive value on it. Nothing else on their own row is writable.
declared_rules: A rule declared on the table itself is the app's policy and is applied as written, per operation: `access: { company_members: { write: role:company_admin,manager, update: role:company_admin, delete: role:company_admin } }`. Declaring `write/update/delete: group` restores tenant-wide member management (any member can add, edit and remove members - only for apps where every member is trusted). The global `default:` block is not a declaration for this table.
not_affected: Flows, hooks, cron, approved commands, operator SQL, POST /api/_groups/create and the member-of founder auto-join write the table themselves. An invite or role-change flow that checks who is asking stays the recommended shape for anything beyond what an access rule can express (workflow transitions on the table follow workflows.yaml).
